book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Hymn for two kings in new Catholic mass

indicators.note: in new reads as 'in a new form', so the two kings and the words Catholic mass are mixed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king, so two kings give two Rs
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seasonal hymn is sung for two monarchs at a Catholic mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The kings join the letters of CATHOLIC MASS, and 'in new' rearranges the whole pool of fourteen letters at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas carol is a festive song of praise, so it is an example of a hymn.

clue.text: Get back to give the suite an update

definitions.meaning: first meaning: regain, retrieve something lost
second meaning: put new upholstery on a sofa and armchairs

explanation.surface: A hotel or furniture owner reclaiming money spent refreshing a suite.
explanation.walkthrough: A suite here is a three-piece set of sofa and armchairs; giving it fresh fabric is to re-cover it, which is spelt the same as the word for getting back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain possession of something, and also, split as re-cover, to fit a new covering.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an attempt, as in 'have a go'
second meaning: a jab from a needle, as a vaccination

explanation.surface: A nurse attempting to administer a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' reads as a verb in the surface but is the noun meaning an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is informally an attempt at something and also a hypodermic injection of a drug or vaccine.

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word for bravery is dropped

parts.note: a fellow is a man
daring is boldness or courage

explanation.surface: A man from China whose bravery never runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese' looks like an adjective for the fellow, but it is the definition: the main spoken language of China.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the official standard form of the Chinese language, so it can stand for Chinese the noun.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: neat and smart in appearance
second meaning: a conifer, the usual Christmas tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' reads as the verb for cutting back a tree, but it is the adjective meaning neat and smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and smartly dressed, and a spruce is also an evergreen conifer of the pine family.

clue.text: A meal's been cooked for mariners

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been prepared and changed, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The ship's galley has prepared dinner for the sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' sits naturally in a kitchen scene, but it is the anagram signal; the surface contraction meal's supplies its S to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Able seamen are ordinary sailors of a recognised rank in the navy or merchant fleet, so they are mariners.

parts.note: surface reading: the perfect catch for someone fishing from a small boat; setter's reading: a deep-sea creature whose name starts with the blade a boater rows with, so it suits a paddler

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a person who propels a boat with a blade would want the long ribbon-like sea creature named after that blade. The question mark admits the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The oarfish is a very long, slender deep-sea fish, so it is literally fare for someone with an oar.

clue.text: The only real alternative for romantic hopeful

indicators.note: an alternative is another version, so the letters before it are made into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone longing for love insists there is only one true option.
explanation.definitionFit: A lonely heart is a person seeking a partner, as in the newspaper personal columns, so a hopeful romantic.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fore-and-aft rigged ship with two or more masts
second meaning: a tall drinking glass for beer or sherry

explanation.surface: A ship that is apparently built out of glass, like a model in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made of' pretends the ship is constructed from glass; it only joins two meanings. In Britain a schooner is a large sherry glass, in Australia a beer glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a two-masted sailing ship and a large drinking glass for sherry or beer.

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: An ancient ship of some size is being eased gently down the slipway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch' reads as part of the ship scene, but here it just joins definition to wordplay: the pieces set the definition going.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical tempo marking meaning slowly and broadly, used as an adverb on a score.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read whimsically: a man who makes trenches

explanation.surface: A labourer who digs ditches is also a big eater.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful reading of the word as one who works on a trench; the real sense comes from trencher, an old wooden plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencherman is someone who eats heartily, from trencher, a platter for serving food.

clue.text: A party where people go wild

definitions.text: A party where people go wild

parts.words: A party where people go wild
parts.note: surface reading: any riotous gathering where guests lose control; setter's reading: a word that as a verb itself means to go wild, to rant, also names such a dance party

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both a noun for a large all-night dance party and a verb for talking or behaving wildly, so the clue hints at itself twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large dance event with loud electronic music where crowds dance through the night.

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of material, so the following letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An English county famous for making porcelain for an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a county known for fine china, such as Staffordshire or Derbyshire, but the words are just raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a county in north-west England, home to Lancaster, Blackpool and Preston.

clue.text: Military body can intercept criminal male

parts.note: a con is a convict
a tin is a can
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: An army unit can stop a man who has broken the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intercept' looks like the verb of the surface; it says the word for can comes between the other two pieces, which is a plain left-to-right order.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group of troops supplied to or forming part of a larger force.

clue.text: Oscar's in trouble because of drowsiness

indicators.note: being in trouble means being in disorder, so the letters before it are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone named Oscar got into a scrape by nodding off.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes 'Oscar's in' as its fodder, so 'in' does double work in the surface but supplies two letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is a state of stupor or deep sleepiness, typically induced by drugs.

clue.text: Tom gets fodder from China of old

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
hay is dried grass fed to animals

explanation.surface: A tomcat is fed on hay imported from ancient China.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the old European name for China, used by Marco Polo and in medieval writing.

clue.text: Gourmands are going to take left-overs

parts.note: greedy eaters are called pigs
will marks the future tense

explanation.surface: Greedy diners intend to polish off whatever food remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is kitchen waste and scraps fed to pigs, so it is literally left-over food.

parts.note: HE, His Eminence, is the formal style of a cardinal
arty means affectedly artistic

explanation.surface: A strong-minded church cardinal with showy, affected artistic leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' tempts as a number or the colour red; here it is the title His Eminence.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty describes someone vigorous and strong, as in a hearty appetite or a hale and hearty person.

parts.note: surface reading: famously full of energy; setter's reading: in terms of musical notes, a tempo marking that asks for a brisk, lively pace

explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' is a coined word: not 'notably' but 'as in notes of music', which points to Italian score directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the Italian tempo direction meaning fast and lively, written on a piece of music.

clue.text: Smartarse has ways to get land

parts.note: wise is an old noun for way or manner, as in 'in no wise' and 'likewise'
an acre is a measure of land, and acres can mean land generally

explanation.surface: A know-all with cunning methods manages to acquire property.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic noun wise (manner, way) survives in likewise, otherwise and 'in no wise'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who pretends to great knowledge, a know-all, which is what smartarse means in slang.

clue.text: Weapon used to lacerate young woman

parts.note: to lacerate is to cut or gash
a lass is a girl or young woman, a Scottish and northern English word

explanation.surface: A blade that was used to slash a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short broad sword with a curved blade, the classic sailor's or pirate's weapon.

clue.text: German takes cover when piloting it

definitions.note: a definition of the craft by its use: what you are in when piloting it

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it within, so the word for cover sits inside the other piece

parts.note: Ger is the standard abbreviation for German
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A German airman ducks for shelter while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is oblique: 'it' is the aircraft being piloted, and the clue leaves the solver to supply which one.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an engineless aircraft, so it is the thing someone flies when piloting one.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
less is used as 'not any more', as in no less

explanation.surface: Determined troops have given up their fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' looks like a past verb (followed), but it is the adjective meaning stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentless means persisting without letting up, which is what dogged determination describes.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a celebrated, admired leading figure
second meaning: a luminous celestial object in the night sky

explanation.surface: A champion who also happens to have a gorgeous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' plays on a beautiful physique, but it means an object in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a famous leading performer or hero and also a sun-like celestial object shining at night.

parts.note: le is French for the
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: France decorates the Polish leader with an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a forename by its famous bearer: Lech Walesa led Poland's Solidarity movement and became president. The stray opening quote mark is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Lech is the first name of Walesa, the Polish union leader, so his surname clues it as an example.

clue.text: Old invader either acute. or obtuse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of a Germanic people who settled in Britain after the Romans
second meaning: in geometry, the opening between two lines, sharp or wide

explanation.surface: An ancient raider who could be either sharp-witted or dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Acute and obtuse look like descriptions of the invader's intelligence; they are the two kinds of geometric opening. The stray full stop is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were one of the peoples who invaded Britain and gave England its name; an angle is also acute or obtuse.

wordplay.note: two words for a road, one often seen in street names as Dr, the other as in a motorway, joined end to end

explanation.surface: The question of which of two roads leads up to the big house.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks for two separate words that each mean road; together they make the private approach. The question mark flags that a mansion is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is the private road leading from the street up to a house, the approach to a mansion.

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters after it are presented in a false order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A doctoral student's research distorted some account of a trial in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctoral thesis is the long dissertation a candidate writes to earn a doctorate such as a PhD.
